card.name: An Dro
card.era: Traditional; revived from the 1950s in fest-noz
card.tagline: Breton round/chain dance from the Vannetais, pinky-linked.
card.profile: An dro (Breton 'the turn') is a Breton folk dance in 4/4, a form of circle/chain dance originating in the pays Vannetais of southern Lower Brittany (Wikipedia). Dancers form a long open line (or couples in cortege, then called kas a-barh), joined by hooking their little fingers and swinging the arms; the step takes a short move right and a longer move left so the chain drifts steadily leftward, the leader at the left end drawing spirals. An dro is considered an 'arm dance' (vs. the 'feet dances' gavotte/hanter-dro). It is sung (call-and-response) or played on biniou/bombarde, accordion and other fest-noz instruments. An dro tunes are central to the Breton repertoire from Alan Stivell and Tri Yann to the rock band Matmatah.
card.insight: One of the most widely known Breton dances outside Brittany, performed within the UNESCO-inscribed fest-noz tradition (Wikipedia; UNESCO).
